newsitem.title: USA: MasterCard president warns of challenge to banking.
newsitem.headline: MasterCard president warns of challenge to banking.

text.p: - MasterCard International President Jerry McElhatton on Thursday warned the U.S. banking industry that its role in financial services was being threatened by newcomers riding the new technology wave.
"I came here to sound a wake-up call about the future of your bank," McElhatton told the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago's Conference on Bank Structure and Competition.

"Technology is changing where we are going, how we will get there and what we'll do once we arrive," said McElhatton, who elaborated on how shopping and transactions on networks such as the Internet is changing the banking businesss.
"I believe that the financial services business is facing a fundamental upheaval in both structure and delivery," the MasterCard president told an audience of bankers and regulators.
"The old lines between banking, insurance and financial markets are blurring. Non-banks are in your markets," he said.

"What it all means is that technology is causing the remaking of money and the payments system... It means that banks will be competing with firms that far removed from banking as we know it today," McElhatton said.
McElhatton said technological advances would cause banks to lose the crucial role they play unless they understand how to use the changes to their advantage, he said.
He identified information on customers using electronic transactions as a potentially valuable asset for financial services providers that can adapt to new technology.
"The key is leveraging information about customers to enhance profitability -- the information that banks may already have," he said.
MasterCard has a program that allows its members "to turn data into information they can use to target their credit card marketing programs... one of the best uses of data mining in the industry."
McElhatton said his company this year planned to have 40 pilot projects in 19 countries in place to develop electronic commerce.
